slug: give_no_quarter
title: Give No Quarter
authors: Trey
season: FF4
format: prose
---

The wide halls echoed with the sounds of electronic beeping and heavy footsteps. Despite their recent successful attack, the Ravens did not bother celebrating. There was always something to be done, and after the last few weeks of being on GU News every night, it seemed optimal to keep the momentum. However, the two remaining Ravens did not party nor toil. They sat in silent darkness on their small warship, biding their time.

Odran’s eyes stayed glued to the glowing holovision, rewinding the same clip over and over. It was hard to believe what he was seeing. He had seen many things during his time with the insurgent group, but this—this was puzzling, and it nearly made Odran nauseous.

“[The footage you are seeing is of today’s terrorist attack on the Fort Gallite GU Military Base, where Major Bobed Ustrrot, notable for his war developments, was killed. It is believed that this was organized by the infamous terrorist group, the Ravens. No other casualties have been confirmed, largely due in part to an unexpected team of fearless individuals. Though currently unidentified, these heroes rushed into the building and rescued other victims as—]{C666666}”

The news report halted as Odran motioned at the HV. “[**Three GUYs of successful operations. Six GUYs of holding the top ranking in the mafia before. But even with that, she’s defeated by a bunch of pests sent by the galaxy’s greatest propaganda machine**]{C990000},” Odran pondered aloud. He nearly choked when he saw Sascha on the news the day before. Not in a million years could Odran have anticipated this outcome.

“**Have you found anything?**” said the Ravens’ leader, in a low, thick voice.

“[**Nothing new, sir**]{C990000},” said Odran, looking up at the screens overhead. He was not as good as Sascha at deciphering the diagnostics, but he knew what it ultimately meant. “[**I don’t know how, but their fleet somehow made it out alive, taking Sascha’s body with them! The armor is nowhere to be found, so they must have destroyed it, or she took it off—but why would she do that!? There must be some explanation, I just need—**]{C990000}”

The boss held his stare at the screens, unmoving. “**Odran, tell me if Sascha is alive.**”

“[**Well…**]{C990000}” Odran stammered, “[**I just can’t be sure. By all accounts she should be dead. Somehow, though, her body is still sustaining itself. Those implants she was so adamant about keeping—they’re reporting damage to the brainstem and central nervous system. These are** ***fatal wounds!***]{C990000}” Odran stood and practically screamed his thoughts at his superior, pointing to the computer as if it had slighted him.

“**Odran**,” the leader rumbled deeply, with a tone that would cause even the hardest hearts to miss a beat.

“[**Y-yes sir?**]{C990000}”

“**How long have we known each other?**”

“[**It’s been…**]{C990000}” Odran paused to think, before continuing, “[**...eighteen thousand, six hundred and twenty-three rotations since I was assigned to your wing, sir.**]{C990000}”

“**And how many times have we failed an operation?**”

“[**Sir, it’s…**]{C990000}” the red-clad Raven paused again, thinking deeper this time, “[**I don’t know.**]{C990000}”

“**Failure is a thing of the past. Failure is a weakness you grow out of, and you surpass it. If you don’t—you die. This is the natural order of things. Death is the ultimate form of defeat**,” growled the shadowed captain, “**but Sascha is above that.**”

“[**What are you implying, sir?**]{C990000}”

“**You were right about one thing. Sascha has never been defeated. Even in death, she fights with an unmatched vigor. That is why she joined us all those years ago**,” the leader explained.

“[**What do you want me to do?**]{C990000}”

“**Find these Horizoners. Kill them, but** ***do not*** **engage directly. That is not a risk we can afford to take**,” said the boss, preparing some device on the opposite wall. “**Use every resource available. Confirm they are dead, and retrieve Sascha if possible.**”

“[**Yes sir.**]{C990000}”

Odran left the intelligence booth and headed for the armory, with blazing determination in his eyes. This had surely been the final nail in the coffin. If there ever was a time for the Horizoners to redeem themselves, or a chance to obtain forgiveness—it had passed and been forgotten. The crew had twice stood in the way of the Ravens, and they would pay dearly for that mistake.

The Ravens would wreak their vengeance.

And give no quarter.
